question: Can the 200 kWp proposal proceed as currently specified, and what changes or conditions are needed?
key_constraints: The roof needs the identified reinforcement before installation because the proposed array load exceeds the stated existing capacity. The 180 kW AC inverter also requires effective export control to keep exports within the utility's 30 kW limit; the stated minimum daytime demand alone does not establish that exports will always remain within that limit.
project_context: A distribution warehouse has 1,200 m² of roof area available after fire lanes and rooftop equipment are excluded. The initial proposal is a 200 kWp array with a 180 kW AC inverter. A preliminary structural review found that the roof can support an additional load of 0.12 kN/m², while the proposed array would impose 0.16 kN/m²; the structural engineer has identified a feasible reinforcement approach, but it has not been completed or approved for construction. The utility has approved a maximum export of 30 kW. The warehouse's recorded daytime demand is at least 120 kW, and the design can use an export-control system. The planned layout avoids the roof section shaded by a neighboring building.
reasoning_answer: The project is conditionally feasible, but the proposal should not proceed unchanged. The proposed array's stated load of 0.16 kN/m² exceeds the roof's current additional-load capacity of 0.12 kN/m², so the identified reinforcement must be completed and approved before installation. The utility permits up to 30 kW of export, so the design must include a suitable export-control arrangement and be checked against that limit under operating conditions. The shaded roof section is excluded from the layout, and the remaining area is stated to be available. With the structural work completed and export compliance confirmed, the project can proceed subject to those conditions.
